input.reasoning:
Estimation approach: Story points converted to engineering hours using a baseline of ~6 hours/point for a blended team (typical mid-complexity SaaS features), then split across roles based on task nature (backend-heavy, frontend-heavy, infra, QA, migration). Total points = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21 = 81 points.

Role split logic per task:
- PW-1 (CI/staging, 5pt): DevOps-heavy, some Backend.
- PW-2 (Design system, 8pt): Frontend-heavy, light QA.
- PW-3 (Registration/login, 8pt, Urgent): Backend-heavy, Frontend, QA.
- PW-4 (RBAC, 13pt, High): Backend-heavy, Frontend, QA.
- PW-5 (Dashboard, 8pt, High): Frontend-heavy, Backend, QA.
- PW-6 (Invoice list/detail, 5pt, Medium): Frontend + Backend, QA.
- PW-7 (Payment integration, 13pt, Urgent): Backend-heavy, DevOps (webhooks/infra), QA (critical path).
- PW-8 (Legacy migration, 21pt, High): Backend-heavy (ETL scripts), DevOps (infra/cutover), QA (data validation).

Hours per point baseline ~6h blended; allocated across roles per task weighting. Totals computed then checked against FTE capacity over an assumed 3-month (13-week, ~520 hours/role at 1.0 FTE) delivery window:
- Backend Developer: 1.5 FTE => ~780 hours capacity over 13 weeks.
- Frontend Developer: 1.0 FTE => ~520 hours capacity.
- QA Engineer: 0.6 FTE => ~312 hours capacity.
- DevOps Engineer: 0.4 FTE => ~208 hours capacity.

Allocated hours (summed across tasks):
Backend: PW-1:10, PW-3:60, PW-4:90, PW-5:40, PW-6:30, PW-7:90, PW-8:140 => 460 hours (within 780 cap, leaves room for PM/overhead & rework).
Frontend: PW-2:70, PW-3:30, PW-4:40, PW-5:60, PW-6:40 => 240 hours (well within 520 cap).
QA: PW-1:5, PW-3:15, PW-4:25, PW-5:15, PW-6:10, PW-7:30, PW-8:35 => 135 hours (within 312 cap).
DevOps: PW-1:35, PW-7:25, PW-8:40 => 100 hours (within 208 cap).

These allocations respect FTE capacity constraints and reflect realistic proportional staffing; QA and DevOps are thinly staffed relative to backlog breadth, so contingency/buffer and phasing risk is flagged.

Non-labour costs: Stripe sandbox/test fees negligible but PCI compliance review, staging cloud infra, and a one-off Oracle migration toolset/license are added. Also project management/coordination overhead assumed absorbed within existing roles (no PM role on rate card) — flagged as assumption.

Priority breakdown computed by summing labour cost of tasks per priority using blended average rate distribution across the hours allocated per task's role mix.

Scenario total (P50) = base labour + non-labour. P20 (optimistic, less rework) discounts ~8%. P80 (pessimistic, integration/migration risk, urgent items slip) adds ~18%.

Reductions identified: descope PW-2 design system to reuse an off-the-shelf UI kit (saves Frontend hours), reduce QA hours on Medium-priority items by relying on automated regression only, defer non-essential PDF export polish in PW-6, and phase Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) to reduce initial DevOps/Backend hours by handling only critical customer records first with invoices migrated in a later phase.

nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration testing / PCI compliance review
Contingency buffer for thinly-staffed QA/DevOps capacity risk

scenarios.name: Optimistic (P20) - minimal rework, no major migration surprises
Most likely (P50) - base estimate as staffed
Pessimistic (P80) - migration/payment integration risk, urgent item slippage, QA/DevOps bottleneck

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; estimate is based on story-point-to-hour heuristics (~6 hours/point blended) and task-type role weighting, not observed velocity.

Delivery window assumed at roughly 13 weeks (one quarter), used only to sanity-check that allocated hours per role stay within each role's FTE capacity (Backend ~780h, Frontend ~520h, QA ~312h, DevOps ~208h available in that window).

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to the breadth of the backlog (8 tasks spanning auth, RBAC, payments, and a large data migration); allocated QA/DevOps hours are proportionate to capacity but leave little slack for concurrent workstreams, so schedule risk is concentrated there.
No Project Manager / Business Analyst role exists on the rate card; coordination overhead is assumed to be absorbed informally by the existing engineering roles and is not separately costed.

Legacy Data Migration (PW-8) hours assume a single migration pass (400k customer records + 2M invoice lines) with standard ETL tooling; unexpected schema mismatches in the legacy Oracle system could increase Backend and DevOps hours materially (captured in the pessimistic scenario).
Payment Provider Integration (PW-7) assumes standard Stripe Checkout/webhooks integration without custom PSP failover logic; PCI compliance review is a fixed non-labour line rather than ongoing cost.
Priority-based cost breakdown allocates each task's blended labour cost to its stated priority; non-labour costs are shown separately since they aren't tied to a single priority tier.
Story points are treated as relative complexity only; actual velocity may vary once real sprint data is collected, and estimate should be recalibrated after the first 2-3 sprints.

reductions.description: Descope PW-2 (custom design system) in favor of adopting an existing Angular Material/PrimeNG theme, reducing custom component build effort
reductions.effect: Cuts ~50 Frontend Developer hours from PW-2 (70h -> 20h); trades some visual differentiation for faster, cheaper delivery.

reductions.description: Reduce QA hours on Medium-priority items (PW-2, PW-6) by relying on automated regression suite instead of extensive manual test cycles
reductions.effect: Cuts ~15 QA Engineer hours across PW-2/PW-6; increases reliance on existing automated coverage and slightly raises regression risk.

reductions.description: Defer non-essential PDF export styling/polish in PW-6 Invoice detail view to a post-launch iteration
reductions.effect: Removes ~20 Backend/Frontend hours from initial scope; PDF export ships with basic formatting only at launch.

reductions.description: Phase Legacy Data Migration (PW-8): migrate only active customer records and last 12 months of invoices in Phase 1, defer full historical invoice migration to Phase 2
reductions.effect: Reduces initial Backend (~40h) and DevOps (~15h) migration effort and shrinks the migration tooling license need; full historical data becomes a separately scoped follow-on project.

reductions.description: Drop the contingency buffer line if the team accepts higher schedule risk on QA/DevOps-constrained tasks
reductions.effect: Removes the non-labour risk buffer entirely; increases likelihood of falling into the pessimistic (P80) cost scenario instead of P50.
